## The pydisort dependency and binary compatibility (`pydisort>=1.7.1`) {#sec-ch10-packaging}

### Summary

pyharp compiles against the C++ headers and shared library of an installed pydisort, and at run time loads
whichever pydisort is installed. This section states which versions the package accepts, which one CI tests, and
what happens when the version pyharp was built against differs from the one it runs with.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** The pydisort versions pyharp builds and runs against, and the result of mixing them.

**Data.** `pydisort>=1.7.1` (build and run requirement); CI installs 1.7.1.

**Placement.** Build time (CMake finds pydisort) and import time (the extension loads its library).

**Activation.** Always; no option.

**Guarantee / limits.** Matched builds pass; built against 1.7.1 and run with 1.8.13 aborts (Limits layer).

**Evidence.** The Tests layer of @sec-ch10-packaging.
:::

Local symbols: none.

The requirement has a lower bound and no upper bound, so `pip install pyharp` today installs pydisort 1.8.13, the
newest release, while CI builds and tests against 1.7.1 only.

### Derivation

None: this section states facts about packaging and has no equations.

### Numerical method

At build time `FindDisort.cmake` asks the Python interpreter for the installed `pydisort` package and uses its
headers and `libdisort_release.so` (`__disort_determine_version`,
{{< code cmake/modules/FindDisort.cmake repo=pyharp >}}). The extension built by
`setup.py` (`ext_module`, {{< code setup.py ext_module repo=pyharp >}}) records the run-time search path
`$ORIGIN/../pydisort/lib`, so at import it loads the library of whatever pydisort is installed then. Both
`pyproject.toml` lists, `[build-system] requires` and `[project] dependencies`, say `pydisort>=1.7.1`
({{< code pyproject.toml repo=pyharp >}}); the CI job installs `pydisort==1.7.1` with `--no-deps`
({{< code .github/workflows/ci.yml repo=pyharp >}}).

pyharp's DISORT band solver holds a `DisortImpl` object, a C++ class that pydisort declares in its header
(`DisortImpl`, {{< code src/disort.hpp DisortImpl repo=pydisort >}}). pyharp's compiled code fixes the size and
member layout of that class from the header it was built with, and pydisort's library code uses the layout of its
own header. The two agree only when the versions agree. In the 1.8.13 wheel the header declares one more data
member in `DisortImpl` than at the pin, a `torch::Tensor cuda_workspace_` described as reused CUDA scratch
storage[^ch10-pkg-header].

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| version requirement | {{< code pyproject.toml repo=pyharp >}} | `pydisort>=1.7.1` | always |
| find pydisort at build time | {{< code cmake/modules/FindDisort.cmake repo=pyharp >}} | `__disort_determine_version` | always |
| extension and run-time path | {{< code setup.py ext_module repo=pyharp >}} | `ext_module` | always |
| version CI tests | {{< code .github/workflows/ci.yml repo=pyharp >}} | `pydisort==1.7.1` | CI |
| the shared class | {{< code src/disort.hpp DisortImpl repo=pydisort >}} | `DisortImpl` | DISORT bands |

: Code map of the pydisort dependency. {#tbl-ch10-packaging-code}

1. `pip install pyharp` resolves `pydisort>=1.7.1` to the newest release ({{< code pyproject.toml repo=pyharp >}}).
2. Building from source, CMake reads the version and paths of the installed pydisort
   ({{< code cmake/modules/FindDisort.cmake repo=pyharp >}}) and links its library.
3. Nothing records the pydisort version a build used, and nothing checks it at import.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `run_suite.sh` `[S6]` | `tests/test_rayleigh.py` three times per build/run pair | exit 0, no abort | process exit |
| `abi_matrix.py` `[A1]`, `[A2]` | the matrix of @fig-ch10-packaging-matrix | exact counts | `[S6]` lines |

: Checks of the pydisort dependency. {#tbl-ch10-packaging-tests}

No pyharp test runs against more than one pydisort version. The test `tests/test_rayleigh.py` builds a
`RadiationBand` with the DISORT solver, so it constructs and destroys a `DisortImpl`. Each of the four pairings
was run three times: built against 1.7.1 and run with 1.7.1, 3 clean; built against 1.8.13 and run with 1.8.13,
3 clean; built against 1.8.13 and run with 1.7.1, 3 clean; built against 1.7.1 and run with 1.8.13, both tests
pass and then the process aborts with `double free or corruption (!prev)` (exit 134) in 3 of 3
runs[^ch10-pkg-runs]. Apart from the intermittent spectra failure described in @sec-ch10-test-suite, the rest of
the suite gives the same results in all four pairings.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
Build pyharp against the pydisort it will run with; a pyharp built against 1.7.1 aborts at exit with 1.8.13.
:::

- **Open bound (CANDIDATE, pydisort compatibility).** `pydisort>=1.7.1` admits 1.8.13, and a pyharp compiled
  against 1.7.1 then corrupts the heap after DISORT runs (3 of 3 runs abort); the matched pairs and the
  1.8.13-built, 1.7.1-run pair do not[^ch10-pkg-runs]. That the cause is the larger `DisortImpl` of 1.8.13
  (the extra member) is a hypothesis consistent with which pair fails; it was not confirmed with a memory checker.
- **The published wheel.** The same abort was seen earlier with the PyPI wheel pyharp 2.7.6 and pydisort 1.8.13;
  2.7.6 is not the pin, so that run is not evidence for this section, and re-running it at the pin would need a
  wheel built from the pin.
- **Untested combinations.** pydisort releases between 1.7.1 and 1.8.13, and macOS: not provided: no run here
  covered them.
